blockMcqs.question: What is the core rule shared by Clean, Hexagonal, and Onion?
options: Never use any framework in the app
Dependencies point inward, toward business rules
Each layer must have its own database
All logic belongs in controller classes
blockMcqs.explanation: Frameworks and DBs are pushed to the edges; the stable core depends on nothing.

blockMcqs.question: Why does DDD insist on a ubiquitous language?
options: To speed up database queries
To enforce a single coding style guide
To close the translation gap between experts and code
To avoid writing any documentation
blockMcqs.explanation: Most business-software defects come from words meaning different things to experts and engineers.

blockMcqs.question: "Order" means different things in Sales and Shipping. This is:
options: A naming bug to be fixed
Fine — each is its own bounded context
A reason to merge both into one model
A violation of the dependency rule
blockMcqs.explanation: A boundary keeps each model internally consistent, so the same word can differ across contexts.

blockMcqs.question: Which distinguishes an entity from a value object?
options: Entities are immutable; value objects are not
Entities have identity; value objects compare by value
Value objects always have a stable ID
Entities cannot hold business rules
blockMcqs.explanation: A User stays the same user despite changes; two equal Money values are interchangeable.

blockMcqs.question: Why route all changes through the aggregate root?
options: It makes SQL queries faster
So invariants can't be bypassed into illegal state
To avoid defining any interfaces
Because roots are stored in a separate table
blockMcqs.explanation: The root is the only entry point, so rules like "no empty order" always hold.

blockMcqs.question: Why invert dependencies toward the domain core?
options: The core changes more often than infrastructure
Infrastructure changes more and is slower to test
It removes the need for any interfaces
Databases run faster when depended upon
blockMcqs.explanation: Volatile, slow externals should depend on stable, fast rules — never the reverse.

blockMcqs.question: Where does the OrderRepository interface live, and its implementation?
options: Both live in the database layer
Interface in the domain, implementation outside
Both live in the domain core
Interface outside, implementation in the domain
blockMcqs.explanation: The domain declares the port; an outer adapter supplies the concrete tech.

blockMcqs.question: Logic sits in service classes while entities are plain data bags. This is:
options: Proper tactical DDD
The anemic domain model anti-pattern
An anti-corruption layer
Correct use of value objects
blockMcqs.explanation: Rules belong inside the aggregate that owns the data, not scattered in services.
